([[Woodstock, Virginia]]) | college = * [[Rhode Island Rams men's basketball|Rhode Island]] (2018–2020) * [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]] (2020–2022) | highlights = }} '''Tyrese Jeffrey Martin''' (born March 7, 1999) is a former American [[college basketball]] player for the [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn Huskies]] of the [[Big East Conference]]. He previously played for the [[Rhode Island Rams men's basketball|Rhode Island Rams]]. ==High school career== Martin played basketball for [[William Allen High School]] in [[Allentown, Pennsylvania]]. As a senior, he averaged 21.3 points and 11.4 rebounds per game. Martin was named [[Eastern Pennsylvania Conference (PIAA)|Eastern Pennsylvania Conference]] (EPC) MVP, and led his team to its first EPC title since 2006.{{cite web |last1=Fierro |first1=Nick |title=Parkland's Sam Iorio leads Valley's strong All-State basketball contingent |url=https://www.mcall.com/sports/varsity/mc-all-state-basketball-0414-20170414-24-story.html |website=[[The Morning Call]] |access-date=October 24, 2021 |date=April 15, 2017}} He played a [[postgraduate season]] at [[Massanutten Military Academy]] in [[Woodstock, Virginia]] to gain more exposure from college programs.{{cite web |last1=Amore |first1=Dom |title=‘A tough, hard-nosed player:’ Things to know about Tyrese Martin, newest member of UConn men |url=https://www.courant.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/hc-sp-clb-uconn-men-tyrese-martin-things-to-know-20200409-20200408-xruejx5f5zacrim3hnvfakmexa-story.html |website=[[Hartford Courant]] |access-date=October 24, 2021 |date=April 8, 2020}} He committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[Rhode Island Rams men's basketball|Rhode Island]] over offers from [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]], [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah]] and [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]], among others.{{cite web |last1=Koch |first1=Bill |title=Pennsylvania guard Tyrese Martin commits to URI |url=https://www.providencejournal.com/sports/20170913/pennsylvania-guard-tyrese-martin-commits-to-uri |website=[[The Providence Journal]] |access-date=October 24, 2021 |date=September 13, 2017}} ==College career== As a freshman at Rhode Island, Martin averaged 8.1 points and 5.2 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Daniels |first1=Evan |title=Eight schools pursuing Tyrese Martin |url=https://247sports.com/Article/Tyrese-martin-Oregon-Louisville-Creighton-Seton-Hall-UConn-Georgia-Ole-Miss-145537767/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=October 24, 2021 |date=March 30, 2020}} On February 26, 2020, he posted season-highs of 24 points and 16 rebounds in a 76–75 win against [[Fordham Rams men's basketball|Fordham]].{{cite web |title=Martin, Toppin lift Rhode Island over Fordham 76-75 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401170315 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=October 24, 2021 |date=February 26, 2020}} Martin averaged 12.8 points and 7 rebounds per game as a sophomore.{{cite web |last1=Borges |first1=David |title=Tyrese Martin, a big, scoring guard, transferring from URI to UConn |url=https://www.nhregister.com/uconn/article/Tyrese-Martin-a-big-scoring-guard-transferring-15184978.php |website=[[New Haven Register]] |access-date=October 24, 2021 |date=April 7, 2020}} For his junior season, he transferred to [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn]] to play under head coach [[Dan Hurley]], who had recruited him to Rhode Island. During the offseason, he worked a full-time job at a warehouse in Allentown after his mother was laid off from her job amid the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web |last1=Carroll |first1=Charlotte |title='It was just hard to turn down': Tyrese Martin embraces opportunity at UConn |url=https://theathletic.com/1730975/2020/04/07/it-was-just-hard-to-turn-down-tyrese-martin-embraces-opportunity-at-uconn/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=October 24, 2021 |date=April 7, 2020}} Martin was granted a waiver from the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] for immediate eligibility at UConn.{{cite web |title=UConn's Tyrese Martin granted waiver to play this season |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29898842/uconn-tyrese-martin-granted-waiver-play-season |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=October 24, 2021 |date=September 16, 2020}} However, he was suspended by the NCAA for the season opener against [[Central Connecticut Blue Devils men's basketball|Central Connecticut]] for playing in an unsanctioned summer league game.{{cite web |last1=Ostrout |first1=Neill |title=UConn's Martin gets 1-game NCAA suspension |url=https://www.journalinquirer.com/sports/uconns-martin-gets-1-game-ncaa-suspension/article_dd265612-2f90-11eb-a082-9741cf95063d.html |website=[[Journal Inquirer]] |access-date=October 24, 2021 |date=November 25, 2020}} As a junior, Martin averaged 10.3 points and 7.5 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Groller |first1=Keith |title=Around the Valley: UConn basketball standout Tyrese Martin came back home to give back to Allentown kids |url=https://www.mcall.com/sports/varsity/mc-spt-tyrese-martin-uconn-allen-basketball-20210831-3xncaf5lybfbhnaen5apmqoxj4-story.html |website=[[The Morning Call]] |access-date=October 24, 2021 |date=August 31, 2021}}{{cite web |last1=Doyle |first1=Paul |title=Tyrese Martin came to Storrs for the UConn Nation experience. After a pandemic season, he'll get his wish. |url=https://www.ctinsider.com/sports/article/Tyrese-Martin-came-to-Storrs-for-the-UConn-Nation-16320613.php |website=CT Insider |access-date=October 24, 2021 |date=July 17, 2021}} On December 1, 2021, he was ruled out after spraining his wrist several games previously.{{cite news |last1=Ostrout |first1=Neill |title=Ostrout: Mounting injuries nearly lead to insult for UConn |url=https://www.journalinquirer.com/sports/college/uconn_mens_basketball/ostrout-mounting-injuries-nearly-lead-to-insult-for-uconn/article_0cc27a18-529f-11ec-be56-ff1f3f5ded31.html |access-date=December 3, 2021 |work=[[Journal Inquirer]] |date=December 1, 2021}} On December 21, Martin scored a career-high 25 points and passed the 1,000 point mark in a 78–70 win over [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]].{{cite news|first=David|last=Borges|url= https://www.newstimes.com/uconn/article/UConn-tops-Marquette-behind-Tyrese-Martin-s-16721383.php |title= UConn men top Marquette behind Tyrese Martin’s career-high 25 points |work=[[The News-Times]]|date= December 22, 2021|access-date=December 22, 2021}} On March 22, Martin declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibilty.{{cite news |last1=Bethune |first1=Ian |title=Tyrese Martin to forgo extra year of eligibility, enter NBA Draft |url=https://www.theuconnblog.com/2022/3/22/22992018/uconn-huskies-mens-basketball-tyrese-martin-to-forgo-extra-year-of-eligibility-enter-nba-draft |access-date=March 29, 2022 |work=The UConn Blog
